candidates.prompt:
WORLD / SCENE IDENTITY

Masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic. A small northern European village during a snowy winter evening, with old wooden cottages, steep snow-covered roofs, tall evergreen trees, warm illuminated windows, and a narrow footpath winding between the houses.

An extraordinary coral-orange sunset glows behind the village beneath a vast deep-blue twilight sky.

The atmosphere feels peaceful, nostalgic, magical, intimate, and deeply wintry.

MAIN VISUAL ANCHOR

One traditional wooden cottage with a steep snow-covered roof stands prominently in the middle ground, slightly right of center.

The house has dark weathered timber walls, a broad triangular roof, small rectangular windows glowing with warm amber light, and a brick chimney releasing a thick column of smoke.

Behind the house, an immense opening of luminous coral, orange, and peach light illuminates the evening sky.

The dark roof silhouette against the glowing horizon provides the strongest architectural contrast.

SECONDARY ANCHOR / HUMAN PRESENCE

Two people walk away from the viewer along the snowy village path.

One adult and one child, both wearing dark winter coats, stand close together near the lower-middle portion of the composition.

Their silhouettes remain small compared with the surrounding houses and trees.

They walk naturally toward the illuminated village, leaving a subtle sequence of footprints in the snow.

COMPOSITION / VISUAL ROUTE

Use a vertical environmental composition from natural standing height.

Build one clear visual route:

foreground deep-blue snow
-> narrow path and footprints
-> two walking figures
-> warm cottage windows
-> central snow-covered roof
-> rising chimney smoke
-> enormous coral-orange sunset clouds
-> deep cobalt-blue evening sky.

The path begins near the lower center and curves gently between the snowbanks toward the illuminated houses.

Tall snow-covered evergreen trees frame both sides of the scene.

Keep the horizon relatively low, allowing the dramatic sky to dominate the upper composition.

CAMERA / FRAMING

Position the camera several meters behind the two figures at natural standing height.

Look gently uphill through the village toward the glowing horizon.

Preserve the complete central cottage, surrounding snow-covered trees, both figures, and substantial open sky.

FOREGROUND / SNOW

Use deep accumulated winter snow with irregular soft surfaces, rounded snowbanks, shallow footprints, and subtle wind-shaped variations.

The nearest snow remains predominantly saturated cobalt blue and deep blue-violet.

Selected upper surfaces catch faint lavender and coral reflected light from the sky.

Keep the snow organized into broad readable forms with restrained surface detail.

MIDDLE GROUND / VILLAGE

Use several modest traditional wooden cottages arranged naturally along the winding path.

The houses have:

weathered dark timber walls,
steep pitched roofs,
thick snow accumulation,
small glowing windows,
simple wooden doors,
and practical rural proportions.

Warm amber light shines through selected windows.

The illumination reaches nearby snowbanks and wooden walls, forming small localized pools of pale gold and soft orange.

Keep the houses irregularly spaced and partially framed by tall evergreen trees.

CHIMNEY SMOKE

A thick column of smoke rises from the central cottage chimney.

The smoke initially ascends vertically before bending gently toward the upper right.

It forms a broad irregular plume, with softly curling edges and translucent overlapping layers.

The lower smoke remains darker blue-gray against the bright sunset.

Its outer edges catch coral and warm orange light where they overlap the illuminated sky.

Keep the smoke physically connected to the chimney.

BACKGROUND / FOREST

Dark spruce and pine trees surround the village.

Their snow-covered branches form deep blue silhouettes against the brighter atmosphere.

More distant cottages and tree groups gradually soften into lavender-blue evening haze.

Preserve clear separation between the dark trees, illuminated houses, and open sky.

SKY / LIGHT EVENT

Use one extraordinary winter sunset event.

The upper sky remains deep cobalt blue, gradually transitioning into muted indigo and blue-violet.

Near the horizon, enormous irregular cloud formations glow with:

vivid coral,
warm salmon pink,
bright orange,
soft peach,
and pale golden cream.

The strongest warm illumination remains concentrated behind the central cottage.

The upper edges of the glowing clouds blend gradually into cooler violet and blue-gray shadow masses.

The last sunlight catches:

the chimney smoke,
selected roof edges,
upper snowbanks,
tree branches,
and distant atmospheric haze.

The warm glow reflects subtly from the snow surfaces facing the horizon.

Shaded snow retains rich cobalt-blue and blue-violet colors.

LIGHT / REFLECTION LOGIC

Use three distinct illumination relationships.

COLD TWILIGHT AMBIENT:

Deep blue skylight illuminates the snow, wooden houses, evergreen branches, and shaded surfaces.

WARM SUNSET BACKLIGHT:

Coral-orange light behind the village outlines selected roof edges, tree silhouettes, and the drifting smoke.

LOCAL WINDOW LIGHT:

Small amber windows cast restrained warm illumination onto immediately adjacent walls and snow.

The snow reflects these local lights as soft broken golden patches that fade naturally with distance from the windows.

Maintain physically coherent light direction, broad feathered transitions, luminous readable middle values, and open chromatic shadows.

COLOR HIERARCHY

BASE:
deep cobalt blue, midnight navy, blue-violet, dark spruce green, cool slate.

COUNTER:
coral orange, warm peach, salmon pink, luminous amber.

ACCENT:
small golden-yellow windows and pale warm reflections on nearby snow.

Preserve strong separation between the cool snow, dark forest silhouettes, and intensely warm sunset clouds.

DEPTH / DETAIL HIERARCHY

foreground snowbank overlap,
path convergence,
human scale,
house repetition,
evergreen layering,
chimney smoke,
and atmospheric softening toward the horizon.

Keep the central cottage, nearest snowbanks, and walking figures clearly readable.

Secondary buildings simplify naturally.

Distant trees and rooftops become subdued silhouettes within the blue-violet atmosphere.

GLOBAL VISUAL LANGUAGE

two people walk through a quiet snow-covered village beneath a vast cobalt-blue evening sky, while an extraordinary coral-orange sunset glows behind the wooden cottages and warm windows illuminate the winter darkness.

The path provides the visual route.

The two figures provide emotional presence and scale.

The central cottage provides the architectural anchor.

The contrast between blue winter snow and the fiery sunset provides the main visual event.
